The taxonomic reference format taxonAlign matches against

Source: R/taxonomic_reference_schema.R
taxonomic_reference_schema.Rd

Describes the columns a taxonomic reference table needs before it can be passed to prepare_taxonomic_resources(), align_taxa(), update_taxa() or create_taxonomic_update_lookup(). Every reference taxonAlign loads (load_taxonomic_resources()) is in this format, and any table you build yourself – by hand, with your own scripts, or with the taxonAlign.dataprep package – just needs to be in it too.

Usage

taxonomic_reference_schema()

Value

A tibble with one row per column: column, required (logical), darwin_core (the Darwin Core name it's renamed from, or NA) and description.

Details

Eight columns are required: canonical_name, scientific_name, taxon_rank, taxonomic_status, taxonomic_dataset, genus, taxon_ID and accepted_name_usage_ID. The names follow APCalign's own; where a Darwin Core name exists (canonicalName, taxonRank, ...), prepare_taxonomic_resources() renames it automatically.

Any other column is kept. A character column named after a rank (family, order, tribe, ...) is read as that rank's value for each row: prepare_taxonomic_resources() adds a row for every family/order/... named this way that has no row of its own. Such an added row's taxon_ID is <taxonomic_dataset>_<rank>_<name>, e.g. "WCVP_family_Annonaceae" (the dataset of the first row naming it) – built from the name alone, so it's the same every time the same reference is prepared. The optional columns listed by taxonomic_reference_schema() (scientific_name_ID, scientific_name_authorship, taxon_distribution, extinct, ...) are never read as ranks. extinct (logical) is described in load_taxonomic_resources().

One record per row. A synonym (any taxonomic_status other than "accepted") has its own row, whose accepted_name_usage_ID is the taxon_ID of the accepted record it leads to. If a table has several references in it, it's ordered from most to least preferred: when the same name appears twice with the same status, taxonAlign uses the first.

See also

check_taxonomic_reference() to check a table is in this format.

Examples

taxonomic_reference_schema()
#> # A tibble: 21 × 4
#>    column                 required darwin_core         description              
#>    <chr>                  <lgl>    <chr>               <chr>                    
#>  1 canonical_name         TRUE     canonicalName       "The name without author…
#>  2 scientific_name        TRUE     scientificName      "The name with authorshi…
#>  3 taxon_rank             TRUE     taxonRank           "The record's rank, e.g.…
#>  4 taxonomic_status       TRUE     taxonomicStatus     "\"accepted\" for a curr…
#>  5 taxonomic_dataset      TRUE     NA                  "The reference the recor…
#>  6 genus                  TRUE     NA                  "The genus of a genus-ra…
#>  7 taxon_ID               TRUE     taxonID             "An identifier for the r…
#>  8 accepted_name_usage_ID TRUE     acceptedNameUsageID "The taxon_ID of the acc…
#>  9 name_type              FALSE    nameType            "Optional; kept as-is."  
#> 10 pro_parte              FALSE    proParte            "Optional; kept as-is."  
#> # ℹ 11 more rows
